core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Jumah corresponds to the Arabic form جمعة (Arabic root ج م ع (j-m-ʿ); جُمُعَة (Jumuʿa)). Its core sense is friday; the day of congregation. Jumah is Arabic جُمُعَة (Jumuʿa) 'Friday; the day of congregation', from the root ج م ع (j-m-ʿ). The source gloss 'Assembly or Congregation' is broadly consistent. Same name as jumaa and jumaat.

faq.a: Jumah is associated with the Arabic form جمعة, whose core sense is friday; the day of congregation.

faq.q: What is the origin of Jumah?
faq.a: Jumah is associated with Arabic. Jumah is Arabic جُمُعَة (Jumuʿa) 'Friday; the day of congregation', from the root ج م ع (j-m-ʿ). The source gloss 'Assembly or Congregation' is broadly consistent. Same name as jumaa and jumaat.
Yes — the underlying form جمعة is Arabic.
Jumah can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Jumah should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. False

faq.q: What does Jumah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Jumah is rendered جمعہ and carries the sense جمعہ، جمعے کا دن.

faq.q: What does Jumah mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Jumah is rendered جمعه and carries the sense جمعه، روز آدینه.
A romanized syllable approximation is ju-mah. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Jumah?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Jumah, jumah. Script forms are جمعة, جمعه, جمعہ, जुमा.

faq.q: Is Jumah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
